newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CMN reduces 1997 savings profits - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CMN reduces 1997 savings profits - paper.

text.p: The National Monetary Council (CMN) decided to raise Brazil's Reference Rate (TR) discount for 1997's first three months, lowering savings account profits for that period, local newspapers said.
The CMN raised the TR discount from 0.85 percent in December to 0.97 percent in January, 0.86 percent in February and 0.95 percent in March, the papers said.
The TR discount is used as a benchmark for savings accounts.
The CMN's decision is aimed at increasing the flow of funds to other investments, such as mutual funds and bank certificates of deposits, the papers said.
